thread:
PagerDuty_bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High tail latency detected for tenant 'OrchardHealth' in dedicated-pool-us-west-2. Severity: SEV2. Pager: @oncall. Link: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-9821
Maria: Orchard health oncall just pinged support — their API calls are timing out (~504) for some heavy batch jobs. Happening since ~08:12 UTC. Customer is on VPC/dedicated pool.
Ana: I’m on it, taking page. Jumping into logs now.
Ana: brief log snippet: `2026-03-15T08:12:34Z tenant=orchard req_id=aa12 tail_lat_p95=1200ms continuous_batch=true max_tokens=4096`
Kevin: Hey, saw page. I’m looking at scheduler metrics for orchard — the tenant has a lot of long-context requests causing max_batch_tokens to balloon and KV cache churn. p50 fine, p95 and p99 are through the roof.
Kevin: Current per-tenant scheduler config: ```tenant_shaper: {max_queue_size: 500, max_batch_tokens: 4096, max_batch_items: 64, scheduling_mode: continous_prefix}```
Eli: We have a queued backlog of ~3k tokens across ~80 requests. The runtime is favoring large-batched windows which increases tail.
Ana: Can we try lowering max_batch_tokens and enable strict per-tenant max_concurrent_batches? Need a quick mitigation before rollback.
Kevin: Agreed. Proposed live tunables: 1) set orchard.max_batch_tokens=1024 2) set orchard.max_concurrent_batches=2 3) enable queue_smoothing=on 4) set per-tenant max_queue_size=200. This should prefer smaller batches and reduce KV cache thrash.
Maria: If we do that will it increase cost or cause more token usage for them? Need to let customer success know expected impact.
Kevin: Might slightly increase per-token compute due to smaller amortization, but latency should drop significantly. Communicate: temporary -> reduced throughput for very large jobs, better 95/99 latency.
Ana: I'm going to run the change as a hotfix on the control plane. If anyone has objections speak now.
SRE Rotation: no objections, +1 for faster p95 recovery.
Ana: executing change: ```curl -X POST https://controlplane.redwood/api/v1/tenants/orchard/config -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"max_batch_tokens":1024,"max_concurrent_batches":2,"max_queue_size":200,"queue_smoothing":true}'```
PagerDuty_bot: Runbook event: applied config change to tenant orchard at 2026-03-15T08:18:05Z by Ana.
Kevin: I'm watching the tail. Metrics show p95 dropping from ~1200ms to ~320ms within 2 minutes. p99 still spiky but trending down.
Eli: KV cache miss rate down 35%, CPU utilization on pool nodes down ~18%.
Maria: Notified Orchard Health support that we applied a tuning change. Message sent: "We applied a temporary scheduler tuning to reduce latency; you may see different throughput on very large batches. We're monitoring and will follow up." :white_check_mark:
Ana: Good. I'm going to hand this to Kevin for follow-up and post-incident analysis. Taking a short break. Handoff to @Kevin for the next 2 hours.
Kevin: Taking over. I'll run a targeted eval on their heavy workloads and propose a safer long-term config — maybe a max_batch_tokens of 1536 + adaptive batching for prefix-heavy requests.
Kevin: Quick note: we should also consider a per-tenant fallback to a smaller model variant for huge requests as an automated SLO-based policy.
SRE Rotation: Marking oncall handoff: Ana -> Kevin at 2026-03-15T08:22:00Z.
PagerDuty_bot: Paging cleared for OrchardHealth incident; severity reduced to SEV3 at 2026-03-15T08:28:40Z.
Eli: I'm collecting perf traces and saving to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-9821/traces/ for postmortem.
Kevin: Capturing experiment notes: 
```
Before: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_concurrent_batches=4, max_queue_size=500
After:  max_batch_tokens=1024, max_concurrent_batches=2, max_queue_size=200, queue_smoothing=on
Observed: p95 1200ms -> 320ms, p99 3400ms -> 980ms, KV_miss_rate -35%, backlog tokens -70% in 10m
```
Maria: Customer message updated: "We applied a temporary config to improve latency. We're running further tests and will propose a longer-term configuration in the next 24h." They replied :thumbsup:.
Ana: Thanks everyone. Kevin — please include recommended rollout: canary for 10% of tenant traffic, monitor eval set, then scale. Also include a replayable perf test.
Kevin: Copy. Will draft RFC and canary plan.
SRE Rotation: closing thread for active paging. Please append postmortem notes to INC-9821 and tag oncall rotation.
Ana: Closing notes: incident mitigated by scheduler knob tuning. Action items: 1) Kevin to RFC adaptive batching + per-tenant model fallback (ETA 48h) 2) Eli to upload traces & perf dashboard (ETA 12h) 3) Maria to coordinate customer comms and confirm SLA impact (ETA 6h).
Kevin: Acknowledged.
Maria: Thanks team :heart:
